summary: A browser game that turns real NASA data into a mission: run a Moon or Mars base, keep your crew alive sol by sol, and learn the actual science behind every gauge, quiz and spacewalk.
details:
You are the astronaut: a first-person helmet view, software-3D base, gloves that move when you work. Pick a real site (lunar south pole or Jezero rim) and keep a crew alive sol by sol, with power, oxygen, water, food, shielding and morale pulling against each other. Learning is part of play: a guided tour teaches by doing, quizzes pay resources and show the fact behind each question, a knowledge passport tracks mastered facts, and a story chapter replays the real May 2024 solar storm from NASA DONKI records so the player shelters the crew before it hits. Twenty-plus trainers cover radio delay, EVA suit reserves, packing an EVA bag, docking, delta-v, launch windows, crew scheduling and radiation shielding. Every real number is labelled with its NASA source in the in-game Sources panel, and every invented number says so.

HOW IT WAS BUILT

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no build step, no server, no network. Open index.html and it runs offline on desktop and phone. Also hosted it as a github pages website version. The first-person view is software 3D on a 2D canvas, with no WebGL or libraries. All in-game audio is synthesised live with the Web Audio API. Progress is saved in browser local storage only. A Node test suite (132 checks) covers the simulation logic. Accessibility: high-contrast mode, reduced-motion support, keyboard and screen-reader friendly lists, and a Voice button that reads tutorial steps aloud.
